Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE REGENT OF BLORA,

Considering : a. that every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, degree and honor and has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence and discrimination as a form of respect, protection and enforcement of Human Rights, particularly the basic rights of women and Children, therefore it is necessary to regulate the implementation of protection for women and Child Victims of violence in Blora Regency; b. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence; In View of : 1. CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Blora Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Kelurahan is a sub-district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the sub-district head's duties.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family parties, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of victims of violence to be able to undertake business/endeavors and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any act against women that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is a woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Companion/Assistant is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to handle and protect Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that organizes Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Children Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the sub-district and village/kelurahan level that organizes protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial condition disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in the community.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and face difficulties in the legal field outside and before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family parties, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

REGENT OF BLORA
DECIDES:
To Establish : REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

Article 3
The objectives of implementing protection for Victims are:
a. to prevent Violence Against Women and Children;
b. to provide services to women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. to empower women and Child Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER XI
CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 27
(1) The Regent shall conduct control, guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence at the regency and Village/Urban Village levels.
(2) In carrying out the control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may delegate it to the Regional Apparatus responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

Article 11
(1) In an effort to increase protection for Victims of violence, UPPA is established at the sub-district and Village/Urban Village levels.
(2) UPPA at the sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by the Sub-district Head by involving community institutions, the Family Welfare Development Driving Team at the sub-district level, community leaders and Child representatives.
(3) UPPA at the Village/Urban Village level as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by the Village Head/Urban Village Head by involving Village/Urban Village apparatus, community institutions in the Village/Urban Village, the Family Welfare Development Driving Team, community leaders and Child representatives.
(4) UPPA as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to provide protection to Victims in the form of:
 a. seeking prevention and handling;
 b. conducting coordination in the context of handling services for Victims of Violence;
 c. seeking increased community participation; and
 d. conducting monitoring and reporting.

CHAPTER XIII
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 30
(1) At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, the institution/network of Integrated Services for Victims of Acts of Violence Against Women and Children of Blora Regency and the Prevention and Handling Unit for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children in Villages/Urban Villages that have already been established shall continue to carry out their duties until the establishment of the institution/network of Integrated Services for Victims of Acts of Violence Against Women and Children of Blora Regency and the Prevention and Handling Unit for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children in Villages/Urban Villages based on this Regional Regulation.
(2) The adjustment of the institution/network of Integrated Services for Victims of Acts of Violence Against Women and Children of Blora Regency and the Prevention and Handling Unit for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children in Villages/Urban Villages shall be implemented no later than 1 (one) year.

Article 23
(1) The form of fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Violence includes the fulfillment of the basic rights of the Child in accordance with their needs.
(2) The fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is the responsibility of the Regional Government, family, and community.

Paragraph 2
Fulfillment of the Rights of Child Victims of Violence

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their natural nature and destiny, without discrimination. In order to prevent and address violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

Article 14
The implementation of protection for Victims of Violence is carried out through:
a. prevention efforts;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

2.3.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, there are explicit elements of a case documentation/reporting system: (i) Pasal 18 ayat (2) huruf a states “identifikasi atau pencatatan awal Korban” (identification or initial recording of victims) as part of complaint services; and (ii) Pasal 9 huruf d and Pasal 11 ayat (4) huruf d assign “melakukan monitoring dan pelaporan” (monitoring and reporting) duties to PPT and UPPA. While the regulation does not spell out a detailed database/IT system, it does mandate recording plus reporting/monitoring functions, which typically satisfies a ‘data collection system’ indicator in policy-scoring schemes. The judge’s cited evidence matches the Indonesian provisions, so the golden ‘No’ appears inconsistent with the source text.

Letter k What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen the Victim, whether physically, psychologically, socially or economically.
Letter l What is meant by "Victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the Victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the Victim.
Letter m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the Victim" is the right of the Victim to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

CHAPTER XI
CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 27
(1) The Regent shall conduct control, guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence at the regency and Village/Urban Village levels.
(2) In carrying out the control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may delegate it to the Regional Apparatus responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

Article 23
(1) The form of fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Violence includes the fulfillment of the basic rights of the Child in accordance with their needs.
(2) The fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is the responsibility of the Regional Government, family, and community.

CHAPTER VIII
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

General

Article 30
(1) At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, the institution/network of Integrated Services for Victims of Acts of Violence Against Women and Children of Blora Regency and the Prevention and Handling Unit for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children in Villages/Urban Villages that have already been established shall continue to carry out their duties until the establishment of the institution/network of Integrated Services for Victims of Acts of Violence Against Women and Children of Blora Regency and the Prevention and Handling Unit for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children in Villages/Urban Villages based on this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER IX
COOPERATION
Article 24
(1) In providing protection to Victims, the Regional Government may conduct cooperation with the Government, the Provincial Government of Central Java, other regency/city governments and other institutions.
(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the government includes consultation, coordination and reporting.
(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government of Central Java includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, return, social reintegration, reporting and development of Integrated Service systems.
(4) Cooperation between the Regional Government and other regency/city governments includes coordination, referral, return and social reintegration.
(5) Cooperation between the Regional Government and other institutions includes coordination, referral, social rehabilitation including provision of Safe Houses (shelters) and social reintegration.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their natural nature and destiny, without discrimination. In order to prevent and address violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

Article 3
The objectives of implementing protection for Victims are:
a. to prevent Violence Against Women and Children;
b. to provide services to women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. to empower women and Child Victims of Violence.

5.3.rationale: The Indonesian text in Pasal 11 ayat (2)–(3) requires involving “lembaga kemasyarakatan” (community institutions) and “tokoh masyarakat” (community leaders) when forming UPPA. However, this is general community participation, not explicit engagement with traditional/customary (adat) institutions, customary law mechanisms, or cultural/traditional leaders as such. The policy does mention “hak asal usul, dan/atau hak tradisional” only in the definition of “Desa” (Pasal 1 angka 4), but that is a generic legal definition and not an implementation requirement to engage adat structures. The judge over-interpreted ‘community leaders’ as ‘customary/traditional engagement,’ leading to a false positive despite the retrieved passages being accurate.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Blora Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of regional government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Kelurahan is a sub-district apparatus formed to assist or carry out part of the sub-district head's duties.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family parties, Integrated Services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Empowerment is the strengthening of victims of violence to be able to undertake business/endeavors and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
10. Violence is any unlawful act that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity.
11. Violence Against Women is any act against women that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child committed by parties who should be responsible for that Child or those who should be trusted.
13. Victim is a woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Companion/Assistant is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Integrated Service is a series of activities to handle and protect Victims of acts of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions and the community as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration and legal assistance.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that organizes Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Children Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the sub-district and village/kelurahan level that organizes protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial condition disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in the community.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and face difficulties in the legal field outside and before the court without compensation.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family parties, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

Article 3
The objectives of implementing protection for Victims are:
a. to prevent Violence Against Women and Children;
b. to provide services to women and Child Victims of Violence; and
c. to empower women and Child Victims of Violence.
